question: What is the primary characteristic of a communicable disease?

options.A: It develops strictly from prolonged exposure to industrial smoke
options.B: It can spread from one person or animal to another
options.C: It cannot be prevented by standard public health measures
options.D: It only affects individuals with chronic genetic disorders

explanation: Communicable diseases are defined by their ability to transmit between hosts, making them a key focus for public health control. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is public health nursing vital during a communicable disease outbreak?

options.A: It shifts focus from individual treatment to community-wide protection
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for expensive laboratory testing
options.C: It guarantees that hospital beds remain entirely empty
options.D: It ensures that doctors no longer need to see infected patients

explanation: Public health interventions aim to safeguard the entire population by breaking transmission chains rather than just treating isolated cases. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h1)

question: An environmental factor that allows a pathogen to survive is part of which element of the epidemiological triangle?
explanation: The environment covers external conditions and surroundings that influence the spread and survival of the infectious agent. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h2)

question: Breaking the chain of infection by washing hands thoroughly targets which specific link?
explanation: Hand hygiene physically removes pathogens, stopping them from moving from surfaces or hands to a new portal of entry. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h2)

question: Giving routine childhood immunizations at a primary health care clinic is an example of which level of prevention?
explanation: Primary prevention focuses on stopping the initial occurrence of disease through measures like vaccination. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h3)

question: A community nurse organizes a blood pressure and blood sugar screening camp for adults. What level of prevention is this?
explanation: Screenings aim to detect diseases early in asymptomatic people so treatment can begin promptly. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of disease surveillance in public health?

options.A: To collect and analyze health data for timely action
options.B: To calculate monthly hospital profits and expenditures
options.C: To punish health workers who fail to treat patients
options.D: To restrict international trade during disease outbreaks

explanation: Surveillance provides the continuous data stream needed to detect, monitor, and respond to public health threats. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why must specific illnesses like cholera be classified as notifiable diseases?

options.A: To ensure patients are charged higher fees for isolation rooms
options.B: To satisfy international tourism requirements for boarding flights
options.C: To reduce the workload of nurses in rural health posts
options.D: To enable rapid public health interventions and prevent widespread outbreaks

explanation: Mandatory notification alerts health authorities immediately so they can contain high-risk pathogens before they spread. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation requires wearing heavy PPE, while quarantine requires no protection
options.B: Isolation is used only for nurses, while quarantine is for medical doctors
options.C: Isolation takes place at home, while quarantine occurs in intensive care
options.D: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine restricts exposed healthy people

explanation: Isolation targets diagnosed, infectious cases, whereas quarantine monitors individuals who were exposed but are not yet symptomatic. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h5)

question: Standard precautions must be applied to which group of patients in a clinic?

options.A: Foreign travelers arriving from epidemic-prone regions
options.B: Only patients who display obvious signs of coughing and fever
options.C: All patients regardless of their diagnosis or infection status
options.D: Patients admitted specifically to the infectious disease ward

explanation: Standard precautions treat every patient as potentially infectious to prevent bloodborne and contact transmission. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h5)

question: What type of immunity is achieved when a high percentage of a population is vaccinated?
explanation: High vaccination coverage creates community-wide protection that shields individuals who cannot receive vaccines. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h6)

question: Why is chemoprophylaxis given to individuals who have been exposed to a specific disease?

options.A: To permanently alter the patient's genetic resistance to bacteria
options.B: To prevent the infection from developing or taking hold in the body
options.C: To cure a severe chronic illness that has lasted for years
options.D: To replace the need for standard hand hygiene in the ward

explanation: Chemoprophylaxis uses medications proactively to stop an established exposure from progressing into an active clinical infection. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h6)

question: Clearing stagnant water around residential areas is a key strategy for controlling which type of disease transmission?
explanation: Stagnant water serves as a breeding ground for mosquitoes, which transmit diseases like malaria and dengue. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h7)

question: How do proper sanitation and safe drinking water primarily protect a community?

options.A: By destroying viral particles floating in indoor air spaces
options.B: By preventing direct skin-to-skin contact between neighbors
options.C: By boosting the antibody production of newborn babies
options.D: By interrupting the fecal-oral transmission route of enteric pathogens

explanation: Clean water and proper waste disposal stop pathogens in human waste from contaminating food and water supplies. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h7)

question: What is the first formal step typically taken when investigating a suspected disease outbreak?

options.A: Writing a final report for international health organizations
options.B: Confirming the existence of the outbreak and verifying the diagnosis
options.C: Demanding the immediate resignation of local health officers
options.D: Closing down all schools and markets in the entire country

explanation: Investigators must first establish whether an actual outbreak is occurring and ensure laboratory confirmation of the disease. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h8)

question: Why is establishing a clear case definition important during an outbreak investigation?

options.A: It ensures all healthcare workers count and identify cases using identical criteria
options.B: It prevents the local government from declaring a public emergency
options.C: It guarantees that treatment costs are covered by international donors
options.D: It allows physicians to skip laboratory testing for every patient

explanation: A standardized case definition ensures consistent data collection so investigators can track the true scope of the outbreak. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h8)

question: What is a key objective of community health education during a disease outbreak?

options.A: Collecting financial levies from households to fund clinics
options.B: Empowering individuals with actionable knowledge to prevent infection
options.C: Frightening residents so they avoid leaving their homes entirely
options.D: Replacing professional medical treatment with traditional herbal remedies

explanation: Health education gives people the practical tools and understanding needed to protect themselves and their families. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h9)

question: Why must nurses consider local beliefs and cultural practices when planning health promotion activities?

options.A: To reduce the number of patients seeking care at primary health centers
options.B: To prove that modern medicine is superior to all traditional practices
options.C: To avoid having to write daily nursing reports for hospital management
options.D: To build trust and ensure the community adopts recommended preventive measures

explanation: Respecting cultural context helps overcome resistance and encourages communities to participate in public health interventions. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h9)
